why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Check 1 tests only that clamp is exported and what it returns for below, above, inside, boundary and lo===hi inputs. "Returns x limited to the range lo to hi" fixes every printed value, so the exact-output match is not stricter than the words. Check 2 requires a RangeError for three cases where lo > hi, which is exactly what the line says. Check 3 requires each exported function to be documented "by name with at least a description". The "add, subtract, multiply and clamp" list follows from the current exports and adds no new rule. Check 4 requires no failing tests and exit code 0. The stricter rules (new clamp tests, `### name(` headings, a meaningful error message) are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)".
